The Chirps and the Welcome Tree

Snail Opens a Sky Museum

“I am opening a sky museum,” Snail announced. Bella flew through the flowers above him. “Where are the pictures?” she called. Snail smiled. “I’m waiting for one to arrive.”

He poked his feelers between the daisies. Petal. Petal. More petal. “How’s the sky looking?” asked Bella. “Like the inside of a daisy,” said Snail. He sounded a little disappointed in the sky.

“I can tell you what it looks like from up here,” Bella offered. Snail tipped his head. “I was hoping to show you what it looks like from down here. My museum is for feet.”

Bella landed and folded her wings. She walked right up to the flowers. Petal. Petal. Her beak tickled. Behind the last petal she caught a tiny triangle of sky. “Oh! Your picture is enormous. Your frame is too small.”

She lifted the flowers to make a bigger frame. For one glorious moment there was sky everywhere. Then the loop slipped. A daisy landed on Bella’s head. “An excellent portrait,” said Snail. “It looks exactly like you.”

“Put the loop there,” he said, looking up at the little wooden peg. Bella hooked it on. The flowers made a great round arch. Snail looked through it a long time. Artists are allowed a long time to look.

Bella took one step. The crooked roof slid into the picture. She took another. Now the sky curved right down to meet the flowers. Snail walked beside her. “You see?” he said. “Every footstep gets its own picture.”

Bella drew the arch on a leaf for the Welcome Tree. She left the middle empty. “Where’s the sky?” she asked Snail, just to hear what he would say. “Open every day,” said Snail. “Come and see.”

Read together

Where would you stand to choose a picture for Snail’s sky museum?
